_comment: The contractor-facing offer — this is who actually pays. Prices are ex VAT per month. Everything here is a commercial commitment, so read it as a contract draft rather than marketing copy: the credit policy and the sharing caps are promises you will be held to. Nothing here claims a network size, a lead volume already flowing, or contractors already signed, because none of that is true yet.
heading: Qualified air conditioning leads, on a flat monthly fee
lede: Homeowners and businesses across London tell us exactly what they want fitted — which rooms, what system, what budget, when. We check the enquiry is real before it reaches you. You pay a flat subscription and keep every penny of the job.
_whyComment: The objection to answer is not 'what does it cost' — it is 'I have been burned by lead sites before'. Lead with that.

why.title: No commission on the job
why.body: You pay for the lead, not a slice of the work. Win a £6,000 multi-split and the price to you is the same as a £1,900 single room.

why.title: You see the brief before you call
why.body: Rooms, approximate sizes, system type, budget band, timescale, property type and any planning constraint. You decide whether it is worth your time before you pick up the phone.

why.title: Capped sharing, not a free-for-all
why.body: A homeowner's details go to a maximum of three installers, and on a territory plan to you alone. You are not the fourth person to ring them that afternoon.

why.title: A dead lead is credited back
why.body: Wrong number, outside your area, already had it fitted, or plainly not a real enquiry — tell us within 72 hours and it does not count against your month.

_qualifiedComment: This is the product. Be specific — 'qualified lead' means nothing on its own, and every competitor says it.
qualifiedLede: Every lead clears all of this before it reaches you. If it does not clear, it is not sent and you are not charged.
qualified: The postcode is inside a patch you have told us you cover
They have said which rooms they want done, and roughly how big
They have seen our published price guide, so the budget conversation has already started
A budget band is stated and it is above £1,500
A timescale is stated and it is inside six months
The phone number is answered or the email bounces back clean — we check before sending
Property type and tenure are known: house or flat, owner or tenant, freeholder consent likely or not
Conservation area, listed building and flat-above-flat constraints are flagged on the brief
It is not a duplicate of an enquiry we have already sent you
_plansComment: Three steps on purpose: free, then per-lead, then subscription. A contractor who has been stung by a lead site will not start on a monthly commitment, so do not ask them to.
plansNote: Prices exclude VAT. No setup fee, no contract, no notice period — stop any time from the dashboard.

_processComment: Contractors want to know how long before leads start and what the vetting asks of them.

process.title: Apply
process.body: Tell us the postcodes you cover, the work you want, and how many leads a month you can genuinely handle. Five minutes.

process.title: We check you out
process.body: F-Gas company certificate, REFCOM or equivalent, public liability cover, Companies House status and two recent customer references. We will not list you without all of it.

process.title: Set your patch
process.body: Choose boroughs and postcodes, set a monthly cap so you are never sent more than you can quote, and tell us what you do not want — no commercial, no flats, whatever it is.

process.title: Leads start
process.body: Usually within a fortnight of approval. Each one arrives by email and SMS with the full brief, and you confirm whether it was any good.

_faqComment: The questions a sceptical contractor actually asks.

faqs.q: How is this different from Checkatrade or Rated People?
faqs.a: Two things. We qualify before we send, rather than passing on anything that arrives, so you are not paying to find out a lead was a tyre-kicker. And we cap how many installers get each enquiry at three, or at one on a territory plan — you are not racing five other vans to the phone.

faqs.q: What happens if a lead is rubbish?
faqs.a: Tell us within 72 hours and it is credited. Wrong or dead number, outside your area, already had the work done, duplicate, or obviously not a genuine enquiry. We would rather credit it than have you stop trusting what we send. Persistent credits on one plan usually mean we have your area or your filters wrong, and we will fix that rather than argue.

faqs.q: Do you take a cut of the job?
faqs.a: No. Never. You pay for the lead and the job is yours — the price is the same whether you win a single bedroom unit or a whole-house multi-split.

faqs.q: How many leads will I actually get?
faqs.a: We will not pretend to know before we have run your area. That is exactly why the first three are free and why pay-as-you-go exists: you find out what the volume and quality really are without committing to a monthly fee. Anyone who quotes you a confident monthly number for a patch they have not tested is guessing.
You do, from the moment you make contact. We do not contact them again about that job, we do not follow up behind you, and we do not sell them anything else.
No contract and no notice period. Stop at the end of any month. A territory is the one exception — because it locks other installers out of a patch, we ask for a month's notice so we can reopen it.

faqs.q: What do you need from me to join?
faqs.a: Your F-Gas company certificate, REFCOM or equivalent registration, proof of public liability cover, your Companies House number and two recent customer references. We re-check the certificates every year and suspend anyone whose cover has lapsed.

_complianceComment: Non-negotiable. We hand personal data to third parties, so there has to be a lawful basis, a visible notice at the point of collection, and a contract with each contractor covering what they may do with it. Do not launch without the privacy notice and the contractor data-sharing terms in place.
compliance: Homeowners are told, before they submit, exactly how many installers will receive their details
Contractors may use a lead only to quote for that job — no marketing, no resale, no adding to a mailing list
A homeowner can ask us to withdraw their enquiry and we will tell every contractor who received it
Certificates are re-checked annually and lapsed cover means suspension
